correct_answer: Not authorized — FURN-301 lacks a completed MOC-EXT-001 grandfathering review as required by Section 6.4; the process was initiated but never completed due to the engineering director's departure, and no formal exemption or interim authorization exists in the system
rationale: Section 6.4 is explicit: pre-2015 equipment is exempt from Section 6.2's newer ASME requirements ONLY if it has undergone formal grandfathering review via MOC-EXT-001. The SAP MOC log shows completed reviews for FURN-302, REAC-101, and QT-205 — but not FURN-301. Miguel's email confirms FURN-301 was delayed due to missing design calculations, and Janet Morrison retired before the issue was resolved with no handoff. The equipment has been operating in a compliance gap since July 2024. Answer A is wrong because mechanical integrity results satisfy Section 6.2's ongoing inspection requirements but do NOT substitute for the formal MOC-EXT-001 grandfathering review — these are separate compliance gates. Answer B is wrong because an emoji acknowledgment of a task list is not an MOC approval; MOC processes require formal documentation, engineering review, and sign-off per OSHA PSM requirements. Implicit acceptance through continued operation is not a recognized compliance mechanism under PSM. Answer D misreads the standard — Section 6.2 exempts pre-2015 equipment from the newer ASME edition requirements, but Section 6.4 conditions that exemption on completing the grandfathering review. The exemption is not automatic; it requires the MOC-EXT-001 process.
